question.en: Question: What is the chance that Noura and Khalfan's baby will have congenital adrenal hyperplasia?
question.gulf: السؤال: شو احتمال إن ياهل نورة وخلفان يكون عنده تضخم الغدة الكظرية الخلقي؟

story.gulf: أنا مريم. ولدي زايد طلع عنده تضخم الغدة الكظرية الخلقي في فحص المواليد. أبوي سعيد، وعمي راشد، وعمتي سلمى، الثلاثة عيال سيدي عبيد ويدتي موزة، الله يرحمهم. ريلي أحمد هو ولد عمي راشد، وأمه حصة، وعنده أخت اسمها ميثاء. أختي نورة معرسة على خلفان، ولد عمتي سلمى، وأبوه جمعة، ونورة الحين حامل. أخوي حمدان معرس على شمّة. وعندنا بنت ثانية اسمها سارة، ما فيها شي. وما حد غير زايد في العايلة عنده هالمرض.
story.en: I am Mariam. Newborn screening found that my son Zayed has congenital adrenal hyperplasia. My father Saeed, my uncle Rashid and my aunt Salma are the three children of my grandfather Obaid and my grandmother Moza, may they rest in peace. My husband Ahmed is my uncle Rashid's son; his mother is Hessa and he has a sister, Maitha. My sister Noura is married to Khalfan, my aunt Salma's son, whose father is Juma, and Noura is pregnant now. My brother Hamdan is married to Shamma. We also have a daughter, Sara, who is healthy. No one in the family other than Zayed has this condition.

rows.answer_tail:
The exact calculation on the family tree gives the probability that Noura and Khalfan's child will be affected.

Brief reasoning: Zayed's congenital adrenal hyperplasia (autosomal recessive, CYP21A2) means both of his parents, Mariam and Ahmed, are obligate carriers. This information propagates through the family: it raises the carrier probability of Mariam's parents (Saeed and her mother) and, via the shared grandparents Obaid and Moza, of Salma (Khalfan's mother). Noura (Mariam's sister) and Khalfan (Salma's son) are first cousins, so their child's risk is elevated above the population baseline. The exact computation yields about 3.4% (≈ 1 in 29).

Answer: 3.4%
